correctness.rationale: Exact primitive-two-cycle cut parametrization follows from the connected Laplacian kernel; complete-minus-matching cuts have the verified triple binomial expansion. The weighted complete-graph cut measure concentrates exponentially centrally; exact first and second split-edge moments yield a conditional rescaled variance \(O(N^{-1})\), independent mean \(2k/(N-1)\), and uniformly \(O(N^{-1})\) logarithmic error for all \(0\le k\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor\). Therefore the claimed uniform ratio law follows analytically. Two distinct standalone programs check exact counts, cut enumeration and 2,375,520 directly simulated bounded chip vectors. Finite experiments are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The generic cut identity and finite combinatorial specialization are not claimed as independently new. The assessed mathematical novelty is the uniform quantitative exponential matching-defect law for the ratio of primitive chip-firing two-cycle orbit populations. The inspected period, firing-pattern and complete-graph publications do not imply this law; equivalence and stronger-coverage searches yielded no covering item. Historical priority remains qualified by limited access and unindexed literature. A previous uniform bounded-degree deletion law for complete bipartite chip-firing graphs is particularly close in method, but concerns a different graph family and does not establish the complete-graph exponent or quantitative rate. Its overlap has been explicitly excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The deleted matching is a vanishing fraction of all edges, yet changing it alters the count of period-two recurrent orbits by a constant asymptotic factor; a perfect matching produces the nonzero loss fraction \(1-e^{-1}\). The result is uniform in every matching size and includes a meaningful exact complete-graph-to-defected-graph comparison rather than a routine isolated invariant or numeric fit.
